blindSummary: Mixed picture: a strong legal framework with a repeating pattern of police round-ups of trans and gender-nonconforming women in one neighbourhood. This state/province has operated its own anti-discrimination law since 1996, hosts a large visible scene and an LGBTQ-driven tourism economy, and concentrates the administration of the national 1% employment quota for trans people alongside the national femicide/trans-feminicide registry — it is where national state response is most likely to be present. Against that: on 18 September, six months after an unlawful detention, officers from a police station carried out fresh detentions, arrests and arbitrary identifications of trans and gender-nonconforming women in a neighbourhood of the city, writing several up under a municipal bylaw provision for lacking documents and arresting one — activists describe it as 'a new illegal procedure against trans women', the third-plus iteration of the same operation in the same neighbourhood, making it a pattern rather than a single incident. Nationally the climate has turned: 2025 set a record of at least 227 hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity (+62% on 2024, one every 38 hours, the highest since monitoring began ten years ago), 32% of them inside police stations and penal facilities, with security-force violence multiplying from 17 cases (2024) to 64 (2025), trans women the majority of victims (142, 62.5%); federal closures of the equality ministry and the national anti-discrimination institute and dismissals of trans public-sector quota hires further erode recourse.
blindSourceSummaries: An LGBTQ+ news outlet (10 April 2025): trans and trans-feminine activists at a local rights forum (4 April 2025) describe their community's situation under the current administration as 'chaotic, desperate', with growing fear and vulnerability to violence, discrimination and poverty; the administration eliminated the equality ministry (women, gender and diversity) in December 2023, closed the national anti-discrimination body in 2024, and dismissed trans people the government had hired under the national 1% public-sector trans employment quota. The association honours a trans activist stabbed to death in her apartment in 2015 and another who died in 2016.

An LGBTI+ news agency (19 March 2026), national hate-crime observatory data: 2025 was a record year — at least 227 hate crimes based on sexual orientation or gender identity, +62% on the previous year, one every 38 hours (highest since monitoring began ten years ago); perpetrators were mostly security-force members and unknown individuals in public spaces, with beating the most used modality; security-force violence cases multiplied from 17 (2024) to 64 (2025); 32% of 2025's crimes occurred in police stations and penal facilities (including a violent raid on a prison diversity pavilion that injured over 45 LGBT+ people and eight guards detained for beating a trans inmate); trans women were 62.5% of victims (142 cases); 64.8% of cases (147) were physical assaults (+101%), the remainder lethal — 16 murders (10 trans women), 53 structural-violence deaths and 11 suicides; in January 2025 a known stalker burned the home of lesbian activists, and a 55-year-old teacher was murdered in a residential neighbourhood in circumstances bearing hate-crime features the media did not frame as such.
